stem:
Aisha's school holds a tetanus vaccination camp. Her uncle asks how immunity and vaccination reduce serious infections such as tetanus and measles and their spread among classmates.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Vaccination prepares the immune system so the body can fight the disease agent more effectively and serious infections are less likely to spread.
A tetanus shot contains live active tetanus bacteria that cause a full tetanus infection on purpose.
The first natural exposure always produces a stronger immune response than a later vaccine dose.
Children living on the same street must have the same immunity after the camp.

teacher.key_rationale: Vaccines train immunity so serious infections and spread are reduced. Tetanus vaccine is not a full live infection by design in this hinge; later protected responses are not weaker than first exposure as a rule; shared street does not equal shared immunity.
